quote: Theorem 3.1. Let X ∼ DoubleXRama(θ1) and Y ∼ DoubleXRama(θ2). If θ1 ≥ θ2, then X ≤lr Y hence X ≤lr Y hence X ≤hr Y, X ≤mrl Y and X ≤st Y.
family: Double XRama distribution, pdf f(x) = θ^4 (θ^6 + 18θ^3 + 108 + 36x^3) e^{-θx} / (θ^3 + 6)^3, x > 0, θ > 0 (mixture of exponential and XRama distributions)

hypotheses.text: Let X ∼ DoubleXRama(θ1) and Y ∼ DoubleXRama(θ2)
Likelihood ratio order (X ≤lr Y) if fX(x)/fY(y) decreases in x. This implies that X ≤lr Y ⇒ X ≤hr Y ⇒ X ≤st Y ⇒ X ≤mrl Y.

ambiguity: The statement duplicates 'hence X ≤lr Y'. The proof then assumes 'If θ2 ≥ θ1, d/dx ln(fx/fy) ≤ 0', which is the opposite inequality from the stated hypothesis θ1 ≥ θ2, so it is unclear which direction the claimed ordering holds. The proof line ends with 'is (CHECK!!!) in x' — an unresolved editorial note in the published text, and the monotonicity word after 'is' is missing. The section's definition of mean residual life order is printed as 'X ≤mrl Y if mX(x) ≥ mY(x)' (conventionally mX ≤ mY), and the stochastic order definition prints 'FY(x) ≥ FY(x)' (one side presumably F_X or a survival function). The printed implication chain 'X ≤lr Y ⇒ X ≤hr Y ⇒ X ≤st Y ⇒ X ≤mrl Y' includes st ⇒ mrl, which is not a standard implication.
